etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Late Middle English (in the sense “cutting, penetrating”), borrowed from Medieval Latin incīsīvus, from incīdō (“to cut in, cut through”) +‎ -īvus (“-ive”, adjectival suffix). Compare Middle French incisif.
senses: Intelligently analytical and concise. (of a person or mental process)
Quickly proceeding to judgment and forceful in expression. (of an action)
